date_basis: date on the manuscript sheet (Sampson p. 161: "September 30, 1843", representing probably the conclusion of some one day's work; p. 160: "1843 September 30, or perhaps a few days earlier")
kind: perturbation solution (circular orbit; modern observations only)
stated_heliocentric_longitude: 304°.0 (Sampson's reading of the sheet: ""Long. at oppn. of Uranus 1843"")
notes: Adams's own memoir §3 gives no numbers for this solution. Sampson's trial with three ancient observations on the same sheets gave e 0.02543, perihelion 96° 17′ (Sampson 161), to which Adams attached little weight. Sampson's reduction to 1846: 309°.1.

kind: perturbation solution (eccentricity of the planet zero; Uranus's eccentricity included)

date_basis: manuscript note dated "April 28th/45" (Sampson 165); comparison with observations dated 1845 May 19
notes: The manuscript note reads: Mean Long. of Planet at Epoch 270° 54′; Motn in 35 yrs 53° 0′ nearly; Long. 1845 = 324° nearly; Mass 1/6000 of Sun nearly. Final values θ = −53° 42′, m′ = 0.7866.

date_basis: θ = −50° 34′ found "under date Sept. 18, 1845" (Sampson 166); the solution communicated to Challis in September 1845 (Adams, memoir §4; Sampson 146)
kind: perturbation solution (first hypothesis; contains a trifling sign error corrected in S5)
stated_heliocentric_longitude: mean longitude "about the end of Septr 1845" = 321° 40′ (sheet of notepaper)
stated_geocentric_position: "Hence Geoc. Long. at the same time will be 320° 30′ nearly, diminishing about 1′ daily" (sheet of notepaper, Sampson 166)
primary_sources: Sampson 1904, 146, 151 (table IV), 166 (E.III and the sheet of notepaper); Adams memoir §4; Challis, Memoirs 16, 415–416 (that a paper with these quantities was handed to him)
mark: P (Sampson's transcription of the sheet; the sheet itself is in the St John's volume)
notes: The sheet is "very similar to that which he sent to Airy in the following month"; Sampson: "very likely the above sheet is a copy of the communication Adams sent to Challis". Final θ = −50° 3′.2, m′ = 0.86511.

date_basis: Sampson 168: "Adams's communication to Airy of the final solution according to the First Hypothesis was made on October 21, 1845"; Airy: "one of the last days of October, 1845" (MNRAS 7, 129); restated 2 Sept 1846 and in the memoir of 12 Nov 1846 (§31)
kind: perturbation solution (Hypothesis I; final for a′ = 2a)
perihelion_longitude: 315° 57′ (memoir §31; Airy No. 20; Sampson table V) / 315° 55′ (Airy No. 11)
stated_heliocentric_longitude: mean longitude 1 October 1845 = 323° 34′ (Airy No. 11); the memoir gives mean longitudes only
primary_sources: Airy MNRAS 7, 129 (No. 11); Airy MNRAS 7, 138 (No. 20); Adams MNRAS 7, 151; Adams memoir §§30–31 (pamphlet p. 18); Sampson 1904, 151 (table V), 166–167 (E.IV, E.V)
notes: θ = −51° 30′ (memoir §30; Sampson E.IV −51° 30′.5); m′ = 0.82816; mean sidereal motion 1° 30′.9 per 365.25 days (Airy No. 11). The 315° 55′ / 315° 57′ and 325° 7′ / 325° 8′ differences are between printings of the same solution; see the statements file.

date_basis: manuscript note "August 20th, 1846" with θ very nearly −42° 51′ (Sampson 167); Sampson 146: "appears to have been completed at the end of August 1846"; communicated to Airy in the letter of 2 September 1846 (MNRAS 7, 137–138)
kind: perturbation solution (Hypothesis II; mean distance 1/30 less)
primary_sources: Airy MNRAS 7, 138 (No. 20); Adams MNRAS 7, 151; Adams memoir §§47–48 (pamphlet p. 25); Sampson 1904, 151 (table VI), 167–168 (E.VI–E.VIII)
notes: Final θ = −46° 55′ (memoir §47; Sampson E.VIII −46° 54′ 50″), ϖ′ = 298° 41′ (1810) → 299° 11′ (1846), m′ = 0.75017. The last perturbation solution Adams computed before the discovery.

date_basis: letter to Airy of 2 September 1846 (MNRAS 7, 139); withdrawn in direction in the memoir §54 (12 Nov 1846)
kind: extrapolation (no elements computed): mean distance inferred from the ratio of the 1843 errors of S5 and S6
mean_longitude_1846: about 315° 20′ ("which I am inclined to think is not far from the truth")
primary_sources: Airy MNRAS 7, 139 (No. 20); Adams MNRAS 7, 152; Adams memoir §§53–54 (pamphlet pp. 28–29)
notes: Basis: Greenwich 1843 errors +6″.84 (Hyp. I) and +5″.50 (Hyp. II) in the letter; 1843–45 errors in the ratio 5:4 in the memoir. Memoir §54: "I hastily inferred … that the effect of a diminution in the mean distance would be to diminish the mean longitude." Not a solution with elements; the mean distance in AU is a derived figure given here only for comparison.

date_basis: Challis's account dated 12 November 1846 (Memoirs 16, 426; MNRAS 7, 148): elements Adams derived from Challis's positions of 4 and 12 August and observations to 13 October
kind: orbit from observations of the planet (not a perturbation solution)
notes: Longitude of the descending node 309° 43′, inclination 1° 45′; "the other elements do not admit, as yet, of any accurate determination".
